$comment: §52. Discovery names recorded whether or not they became serious. This is not a market landscape and it does not claim exhaustive coverage.

candidates.name: Globalping
candidates.why_considered: §51's bias in order: an explicit arbitrary-target HTTP measurement, its own probe network, per-result job statuses, status and header exposure, a documented request object, and selectable vantage

candidates.name: urlscan.io
candidates.why_considered: an on-demand URL submission service that performs its own visit
candidates.pre_gate_failure: the result surface is a browser page capture -- DOM snapshot and screenshot -- and the Result API reference was not retrievable at the path tried, so no transport-only result path was established. §16 forbids ingesting a body in order to extract a status.

candidates.name: RIPE Atlas
candidates.why_considered: a distributed measurement network run by a different institution, documenting an http type: 'Make an HTTP request to a target. Configure path, method, port, and HTTP version.'
candidates.pre_gate_failure: the HTTP result format and the acceptable use policy were not retrievable at the paths tried -- the result-format page returned 404 and the AUP returned a page with no body. §54 forbids closing a gate from a third party, so the candidate could not become serious.

why_discovery_stopped: the documentation budget was spent, and §2 caps serious candidates rather than requiring five. Two of the three could not clear the documentation pre-gate at the paths tried, which is a fact about this mission's reach rather than a finding about them.
